Compute population exposure to Heat Index by NOAA class

Source: R/exposure.R
hi_exposure.Rd

Downloads the municipal Heat Index table with population data from Zenodo and returns population counts by NOAA thermal class for the requested month, local hour, and census year. Results can be aggregated at the municipality, state, or Semiarid level.

Usage

hi_exposure(
  month,
  hour_local,
  census_year = 2022,
  by = c("municipality", "state", "semiarid"),
  cache_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

month

Integer (1-12). Month of interest. Required.

hour_local

Integer (0-23). Local hour (UTC-3). Required.

census_year

Integer. Census year for population weights. One of 2000, 2010, or 2022. Defaults to 2022. The package applies the following convention: use 2000 for analyses covering 2000-2009, 2010 for 2010-2021, and 2022 for 2022 onward.

by

Character. Aggregation level. One of "municipality" (default), "state", or "semiarid" (total for the entire region).

cache_dir

Character. Cache directory for downloaded files. Defaults to the package cache via tools::R_user_dir().

Value

A data frame with columns depending on the aggregation level:

code_muni

IBGE municipality code (only when by = "municipality").

name_muni

Municipality name (only when by = "municipality").

abbrev_state

State abbreviation (when by = "municipality" or "state").

month

Requested month.

hour_local

Requested local hour.

hour_utc

Corresponding UTC hour.

ic_mean

Mean Heat Index for the municipality (degrees C).

noaa_class

NOAA thermal class: No caution, Caution, Extreme caution, Danger, or Extreme danger.

population

Total population in the NOAA class for the census year.

population_share

Share of total population in the NOAA class (0 to 1).

Details

The NOAA Heat Index classification thresholds used are: No caution (IC below 27 degrees C), Caution (27 to 32 degrees C), Extreme caution (32 to 41 degrees C), Danger (41 to 54 degrees C), and Extreme danger (above 54 degrees C).

Population data come from the IBGE Census. The pop_2000 column covers the 2000 census, pop_2010 covers the 2010 census, and pop_2022 covers the 2022 census. Use the census year closest to your analysis period.

The function downloads the ~35 MB population table from Zenodo on first use and caches it locally. Subsequent calls read from the cache.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Population exposure in January at 15h local time, 2022 census
hi_exposure(month = 1, hour_local = 15)

# Aggregated by state
hi_exposure(month = 7, hour_local = 12, by = "state")

# Total Semiarid exposure
hi_exposure(month = 1, hour_local = 15, by = "semiarid")

# Using 2000 census weights
hi_exposure(month = 1, hour_local = 15, census_year = 2000)
} # }
